one_line: patient-facing SMART on FHIR growth chart for the Epic sandbox
skills: growth analysis implementation (z-score, velocity, corrected age)
data: mock demo scenarios including a Turner syndrome teaching case and a preterm catch-up case

decisions.chose: computing the displayed flags from a height z-score threshold at render time
decisions.over: hand-written trend annotations stored on each demo scenario
decisions.because: the scripted annotations were presentation copy rather than anything the data produced, and they could not survive real record data
decisions.evidence: Percentile labels in mock mode are demo annotations for presentation only.
decisions.source: /Users/dominiero/Documents/GitHub/growthbridge-demo/src/main.ts (removed in commit 916fb06, "Compute height flags from z-score threshold")

decisions.chose: a read-only browser app with no backend
decisions.over: FHIR write-back and server-side auth services
decisions.because: it is a demonstration of the family-facing view, not a clinical product
decisions.evidence: Out of scope right now: - FHIR write-back - production auth/backend services - validated CDC/WHO percentile engine

decisions.chose: keeping home-entered measurements in the family's own browser storage
decisions.because: there is no backend and the data never has to leave the device
decisions.evidence: local browser storage for home-entered measurements

decisions.chose: falling back to a mock scenario when the SMART launch fails
decisions.over: showing a dead end when Epic context is missing
decisions.because: the app has to be openable from a plain link, without a launch context
decisions.evidence: console.error("SMART launch failed. Falling back to mock data.", error);

broke.what: the Turner teaching case had been narrated as a percentile drop that the z-score rule would never flag, so the mock percentiles had to be moved down to values the computed rule actually catches
the GitHub Pages deployment did not work as first written; the workflow needed explicit job permissions, Pages enablement, and newer action versions
Epic's exact redirect matching makes the project-subpath URL a trap, since the site root and index.html are not the same registered value
broke.evidence: Epic requires exact redirect URI matching. - `/index.html` is different from `/`.

broke.what: percentiles are not from a validated engine, and the midparental height formula in the code still has no documented source
broke.evidence: Add documentation for the source and assumptions behind the mid-parental height formula.

broke.what: never exercised against a real Epic sandbox client, and the FHIR parsing and personalization utilities still have no tests
broke.evidence: Add a real Epic sandbox client ID in `.env`. ... Add unit tests for FHIR parsing and personalization utilities.

question: What would it look like for a family to see and understand their child's growth record between visits?
rejected_line: the scripted per-scenario trend insights went away once flags were computed from the z-score threshold, since a hand-written percentile-drop story cannot follow real record data
